title: Child with a cold (ARVI): pediatrician visit
what: The pediatrician examines your sick child and tells you how to treat the cold at home. A cold usually goes away by itself in 5 to 7 days.
why: For a runny nose, cough, sore throat or fever in a child.
duration: the visit usually takes 15 to 20 minutes
tell_doctor: When the symptoms began and what the temperature was
What you gave and in what dose
How your child drinks and how much they urinate
If there is a rash, ear pain or hard breathing

prepare.title: Notes
prepare.text: Write down the temperature and the times you gave fever medicine.

prepare.title: Visit or home call
prepare.text: If the fever is high, you can call the doctor to your home. Ask the clinic.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Clothes that are easy to take off for the exam.

steps: The doctor asks you about the illness
Looks at the throat and nose
Sometimes feels the belly and neck
Explains how to treat at home and when to call again
feel: Looking at the throat can be unpleasant - your child may cry, this is normal
The rest of the exam is painless - you can hold your child on your lap
after: Bring the fever down if your child feels unwell - the doctor will tell you the dose
Antibiotics are usually not needed for a cold - give them only if prescribed
If your child is not better after 3 days, see the doctor again
red_flags: Your child breathes hard or fast, or the skin between the ribs sucks in - call your local emergency number
A rash that does not fade when pressed with a glass - call your local emergency number
Your child is limp, not drinking or has not urinated for a long time - see a doctor urgently
A seizure with fever - call your local emergency number

faq.q: Are antibiotics needed for a cold?
faq.a: Usually not, because colds are caused by viruses. Only a doctor prescribes antibiotics.

faq.q: When can my child go back to nursery?
faq.a: Usually when there is no fever and your child feels well. The doctor will tell you the time.

reminders.text: Pediatrician visit soon. Take the medical record and write down the temperature and medicines you gave.
